extracted.intended_audience: executive branch agency officials responsible for standards, procurement, regulation, and related policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for executive branch agencies on when and how to participate in, use, and coordinate with commercial (non‑Federal) standards‑setting bodies and commercial standards in procurement and regulatory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: rely on commercial standards whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the Federal Government to rely on commercial standards, both domestic and international, whenever feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy is intended to further the Government's general policy of using commercial products and the private enterprise system to supply Government needs (see OMB Circular A-76). Relying on commercial standards will reduce the cost of developing standards and minimize confusion among users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives: maximum use and active participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives are to insure maximum practicable use of commercial standards by the Federal Government and active participation by the Government in development of such standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These objectives are consistent with promoting long-term efficiency for government and the private sector and with coordinating Federal involvement in standards development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: scope of application
rubrics_metrics.description: This Circular applies to all executive agency involvement in commercial standardization activities, both domestic and international.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to executive departments, military departments, independent establishments, and wholly owned Government corporations as defined in Title 5 and the Government Corporation Control Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: executive agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive agency (hereinafter referred to as agency) means an executive department, a military department, and an independent establishment within the meaning of sections 101, 102 and 104(1) of Title 5, United States Code, and also a wholly owned Government corporation within the meaning of section 101 of the Government Corporation Control Act (31 U.S.C. 846).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: commercial standards‑setting bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial standards‑setting bodies are domestic and international standardization bodies, including nonprofit organizations, operating outside of the Federal Government or its agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They do not include the development and adoption of professional standards of conduct and standards of private companies; nor the United States' participation in international standardization activities pursuant to treaties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: commercial standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial standard means a prescribed set of rules, conditions, or requirements established by commercial standards‑setting bodies concerning definition of terms; classification of components; specification of materials, performance, or operations; delineation of procedures; or measurement of quantity and quality in describing materials, products, systems, services, or practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: standardization and standards‑setting activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardization and standards‑setting activities mean the process of developing the rules, conditions, and requirements defined in the commercial standard definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: cooperative testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative testing means testing by interested parties to establish such things as precision, accuracy, and reliability of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation principle: when to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies will participate in commercial standards‑setting activities when such participation is in the public interest and is compatible with the agency's missions and authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation by agency personnel shall have the approval of appropriate officials and shall be consistent with the agency's regulations issued pursuant to paragraph 7a of this Circular, but of itself does not connote agency agreement with or endorsement of decisions reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible forms of agency participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency participation in standards activities may include direct financial support, sustaining memberships, contracts; indirect or administrative support such as travel costs and document preparation or grants; and technical support including standards evaluation and cooperative testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation should be budgeted and approved as appropriate; specific examples listed in the Circular include (1) direct financial support, sustaining memberships, and contracts; (2) indirect or administrative support, e.g., travel cost and document preparation; and (3) technical support, e.g., cooperative testing and standards evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of standards bodies' procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should encourage commercial standards‑setting bodies with which they interact to observe rules and procedures that ensure prompt and full consideration of the views and interests of all who might be materially affected by their actions, and evaluate participation in these bodies in light of their adherence to such rules and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should use adherence to openness, timely consideration, and inclusiveness as factors in deciding whether and how to engage with a standards body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use commercial standards in lieu of in‑house standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commercial standards in lieu of in‑house standards when they will serve the agency's purpose and are consistent with applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give such commercial standards preference in procurement actions unless use of such standards would result in higher cost to the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of applicable commercial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite applicable commercial standards in Federal Register publications, regulatory orders, or in‑house documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should reference commercial standards where appropriate in their formal publications and regulatory materials to promote consistency and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint planning with commercial sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan jointly with the commercial sector to ensure a coordinated effort in resolving priority standardization problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should proactively engage industry and other private organizations to address priority standardization needs through coordinated efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation responsibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will, within six months of the date of this Circular, implement the policy principles in paragraph 6 to the extent compatible with its mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation should recognize the positive contribution of standardization and related activities (product and compliance testing and certification) while also taking steps to avoid potential adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk awareness and legal constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must recognize that standardization activities, if improperly conducted, could suppress free and fair competition; impede innovation and technical progress; exclude safer and less expensive products; or otherwise adversely affect trade, commerce, health, or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full account shall be taken of applicable Federal laws, policies, and national objectives including, for example, laws and regulations relating to antitrust, national security, product safety, and conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination role of Department of Commerce and ICSP
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Commerce shall be responsible for coordinating the implementation of said policy principles through an Interagency Committee on Standards Policy (ICSP) established to foster cooperative participation by the Federal Government and U.S. industry and other private organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department of Commerce, through the ICSP, shall periodically advise OMB concerning implementation of the policy principles set forth in this Circular.
